Replies.Text:
Design, Step 4: Closing and Shutdown. Nine decisions, each with my recommendation first. Resolve with no reply to take them all; reply with the numbers you want otherwise, and I apply the result under "Decided before the build".

1. The prompt. A close-prompt component, one in the page beside the popups, opened by a Closing service: Closing.Ask( Tabs ) returns a promise of save, discard or cancel. It says "N documents have unsaved changes" (or the one's title), lists them by title one per line (a stale one marked "stale, cannot be saved"), and has Save, Discard and Cancel; Enter is Save, Escape Cancel; the backdrop and the styles the Help popup's.

2. Which closes ask. Tabs.Close, CloseOthers, CloseToTheRight and CloseAll (the ×, the menu) go through Closing with the dirty tabs among those to close: none dirty, they close at once; Cancel, nothing closes; Discard, the drafts are dropped and all close; Save, each dirty tab's draft is saved on its root (Tabs.SaveDraft( Tab ): PUT /text with the draft's text and base, the way the editor saves), then all close; a refused save (stale) keeps that tab open with a toast and the rest close. The prune of items that are gone and a detached window's "closed" message do not ask: nothing is left to save for the one, the other's window asked already.

3. The draft is current: Step 3 made the editor write the tab's draft on every change, so a close from the menu finds the text as typed; the active tab needs no flush.

4. The setting. Confirm on close, a checkbox under the Editor select in the look popover (State.ConfirmClose, key confirm-close, on by default, remembered where the Editor setting is). It guards the window's close and the browser's leave prompt. A tab's close asks regardless: it is the one moment the draft can still be saved before its tab is gone, and the owner's thread was about shutdown.

5. The desktop's close. main.js's close handler, instead of destroying the window at once, sends close-requested to its page and waits; the preload exposes ConsensusDesktop.OnCloseRequested( Handler ) and ConsensusDesktop.CloseDecided( Ok ). The page: with the setting off or no dirty tab it answers true at once; otherwise it opens the prompt over its dirty tabs (the main window's; a detached window's one), Save saving them all before answering true, Discard dropping them and answering true, Cancel answering false, the window staying. No answer within three seconds (the servers screen, a page that is broken) and the window closes anyway. Quit closes each window in turn, so each asks. Detached windows get the same handler in did-create-window.

6. The browser. With the setting on and a dirty tab, a beforeunload handler sets returnValue, so the browser shows its own prompt (it cannot list the documents); with the setting off, no handler. The drafts stay in localStorage either way, so Leave loses nothing and the tabs come back dirty.

7. Discard at the desktop's close drops the drafts before the window goes, so they do not come back; a browser's Leave keeps them, since that prompt is the browser's. A close that was not asked about (the setting off, a crash) keeps them, as the parent says.

8. Tests. Browser: a dirty tab's × opens the prompt with its title; Cancel keeps it dirty; Discard closes it and a reopen is clean; Save closes it with the revision bumped; Close all with two dirty tabs lists both, one stale: Save saves one and keeps the stale one with the toast; the setting toggles in the popover and is remembered; the beforeunload handler (called directly) sets a value only while dirty with the setting on. The desktop smoke: a dirty tab, then window.close() from the page: the prompt shows; Cancel leaves the window; the setting off and close again: the app ends, which is the smoke's last check today.

9. Out of this step: the guide (Step 5).

Replies.Text:
Build log, Step 4: Closing and Shutdown. Built as decided, with the notes below; one prompt before tabs with unsaved edits close, on a tab's close and on the desktop window's, the browser's own prompt on leaving, and Confirm on close in the look popover. Resolve to have it committed as "Markdown Editor: Step 4"; reply where something should be otherwise.

What was done

1. The prompt (decision 1): a Closing service (public/js/closing.js: Prompt, Ask( Tabs ) returning a promise of save, discard or cancel, Answer) and a close-prompt component (public/components/close-prompt) in the page beside the popups, in the Help popup's frame and form. It says "“Title” has unsaved changes" or "N documents have unsaved changes", lists the documents one per line, a stale one marked "stale, cannot be saved: the plan moved on since this edit began", and offers Save (off when every draft is stale), Discard and Cancel; Enter is Save, Escape Cancel; the form takes the focus as it opens. A second Ask cancels the first.
2. Which closes ask (2): Tabs.Close, CloseOthers, CloseToTheRight and CloseAll go through allowed( List ): the dirty tabs among those to close are asked about; none dirty and they close at once; Cancel closes nothing; Discard forgets the drafts and closes all; Save saves each draft on its root through the new Tabs.SaveDraft( Tab ) (PUT /text with the draft's text and base; the draft forgotten when taken; a draft-saved event moving the open editor's base on) and a refused one keeps its tab open with a toast ("… was not saved: <the server's reason>; its draft is kept") while the rest close. The prune of items that are gone, a trashed item's tabs and a detached window's "closed" message close at once.
3. The draft is current (3): Step 3 writes it on every change; nothing more was needed.
4. The setting (4): Confirm on close, a checkbox under the Editor select in the look popover (id confirm-close; State.ConfirmClose, key confirm-close, on by default, remembered where the Editor setting is, State.SetConfirmClose). It guards the window's close and the browser's leave prompt; a tab's close asks regardless.
5. The desktop (5): main.js's close handler, for the main window and for each detached window (did-create-window), prevents the close and asks the page: close-requested goes to the window's page, the page answers close-decided, and no answer within three seconds closes the window anyway; the connect screen is closed at once. The preload exposes ConsensusDesktop.OnCloseRequested( Handler ) and CloseDecided( Ok ). The page (Tabs) answers true at once with the setting off or nothing dirty; otherwise it asks over its dirty tabs and answers true when every draft was saved or dropped, false on Cancel or a refused save. Quit closes each window in turn, so each asks, and a Cancel aborts the quit.
6. The browser (6): with the setting on and a dirty tab, a beforeunload handler prevents the default and sets returnValue, so the browser shows its own prompt; with it off, nothing. The handler is not installed in the desktop, where it would cancel a reload silently. The drafts stay in the remembered state either way.
7. Discard (7) at the desktop's close drops the drafts before the window goes; a browser's Leave keeps them, as does a close that was not asked about.
8. Tests (8): a browser test drives it: the × of a dirty tab asks, naming it; Cancel keeps the tab and its draft; Discard closes it and the plan is unchanged; Save closes it with the text saved and the revision bumped; Close all with two dirty tabs, the second made stale by a save from the API, lists both with the stale mark, Save saves the first, keeps the second with its dot and the toast; the setting is on by default, the synthetic beforeunload is prevented only while dirty with the setting on, off and on again through the checkbox and remembered. node --test: 196 pass (195 before: one browser test added), the whole suite run to the end. The desktop smoke: a draft set on the open tab, Quit raises the prompt naming the plan, Cancel keeps the app and the draft, Confirm on close off and Quit ends the app; the whole smoke (page and desktop) ends SMOKE OK with 43 checks, the three new ones among them; its first run stopped before the draft because the desktop page had come back from the servers screen without the plan open, and the smoke now opens it first.

Notes and departures

- The smoke asks through Quit rather than window.close(): a page may not close the main window by script, and Quit walks the same close handler, cancelled by the prompt's Cancel as the design wants.
- The browser test's one console error is the 409 of the stale save it provokes; the test lets that one through.
- The tab-closing functions are asynchronous now, so a close from the strip lands a moment later; the tab tests, which wait for the strip, passed as they were.
- The connect screen (Servers…) is closed without asking: it has no page and no drafts.
- The server tests ran untouched; the guide and the pictures are Step 5's.
